note: AI.md, fixtures for jobs 8 and 9: 'At least thirty documents, including a progress note, a plan of care, a discharge summary, an insurance letter, a referral, a handwritten programme, a badly photographed one, one in Spanish, one out of scope, and one blank.' Each document is a page somebody could be holding in a hallway, written the way on-device extraction hands it over, with the line breaks and the run-on capitalisation left in. 'kind' is what PageKind.of has to come back with. The out of scope ones are why the file exists: a blood test, an imaging page and a prescription must never reach the reader in Part 7, and a badly photographed one of each must not either.

documents.name: numbered-home-programme
documents.why: the commonest page in the app: a numbered sheet with reps and sets under a clinic letterhead
documents.text:
Ashfield Physiotherapy Department
Home programme for Patrick Nolan
Prepared 18 February 2026 by R Amara

1. Sit to stands from the armchair with the cushion taken out. 3 sets of 8, twice a day.
2. Heel raises at the kitchen worktop. 2 sets of 15, both legs.
3. Step ups onto the bottom stair, holding the rail. 10 reps each side, once a day.
4. Standing balance with one foot in front of the other, hold for 20 seconds. 3 times per day.
5. Walk to the postbox and back once a day if the pavement is dry.

documents.name: prose-home-programme
documents.why: a sheet written as paragraphs instead of a list, with the counts spelled out in words
documents.text:
YOUR EXERCISES FOR THE NEXT FOUR WEEKS

Start with the sit to stands. Sit at the front of a firm dining chair with your feet
flat and a little way back, and stand up without pushing through your hands. Do ten of
these, rest for a minute, and do ten more. Twice a day is plenty.

The heel raises are easier and you can do them while the kettle boils. Hold the worktop
lightly, come up onto your toes, and lower slowly to a count of three. Fifteen of them,
each side, once a day.

Finish with the standing balance. Stand close to the sink with one foot in front of the
other and hold for thirty seconds, three times a day.

documents.name: progress-note
documents.why: the progress note AI.md asks for: shorthand written to another clinician, and prose
documents.text:
Ashfield Physiotherapy
Progress note, visit 4 of 8
Date of service: 11 May 2026

Mr Nolan came in today with his daughter and walked from the car park to the treatment
room without stopping, which he has not done before. He tells me he has been out to the
postbox on his own three times since the last visit and that the kerb outside his gate
is still the part he dislikes. AROM at the right shoulder is 0 to 140 degrees and MMT of
the rotator cuff is 4 out of 5 throughout. Gait is steady indoors and outdoors on level
ground, and transfers are effortless from a standard chair.

We read through the home programme together and left it as it is for now.

Ruth Amara, MPT

documents.text:
Ridgeway Physical Therapy
Plan of care
Margaret Doyle          Date of service: 2 March 2026, initial evaluation

Mrs Doyle was seen today following a left total knee replacement on 12 January. She
lives alone in a two storey house with a rail on one side of the stairs and she is
walking indoors without a device over short distances. Transfers from her armchair are
effortful and she uses her arms for all of them at present.

Frequency: 2 times per week for six weeks
Interventions: therapeutic exercise, gait training, stair training, manual therapy
What she came in for: the stairs at home with one rail, and getting out of the armchair
without pushing through her arms, both within six weeks.

documents.text:
Hollis Rehabilitation
Discharge summary
Treatment dates: 3 February to 20 April 2026
Discharge date: 20 April 2026

Mrs Okafor attended twelve sessions after her hip fracture in January and was discharged
today having done the two things she came in for. She walks indoors without a frame and
gets on and off the bed on her own, neither of which she could do at the initial
evaluation. Gait is steady over level ground and she uses a stick outdoors by choice.
ADLs are independent with the exception of the bath, which her daughter helps with. MMT
of the right hip abductors is 4 out of 5 and AROM is within functional limits.

She has been given a written programme to carry on with at home and knows to ring the
department if anything changes.

Daniel Reyes, PT

Meadow Lane Occupational Therapy
Home visit and plan
Date of visit: 3 April 2026

We visited Mrs Okafor at home on 3 April to look at how she is managing in the kitchen
and the bathroom. She is independent with dressing and washing and needs a hand only

ELM ROAD SURGERY
4 Elm Road, Ardmore

Dear Physiotherapy Department,

Thank you for seeing Mr Patrick Nolan, who is 78 and has had increasing difficulty
getting out of a low chair and getting up the stairs at home over the past year. He has
had two near stumbles indoors since the autumn and has stopped walking to the shops on

documents.name: post-operative-protocol
documents.why: a surgeon's handout: paragraphs of what to expect, then the movements, on one page
documents.text:
Northgate Orthopaedics
After a total knee replacement, week nought to week six

You are weight bearing as tolerated on the left leg from the day of the operation, and
the crutches are there for balance rather than to take your weight. Most people are down
to one crutch indoors by the end of the second week and to none by the end of the sixth.
Transfers in and out of a low chair are the hardest part for a fortnight and your gait
will be uneven until the swelling settles, and both of those are expected.

Do these four times a day, morning, midday, teatime and before bed:

1. Ankle pumps, 20 reps each leg
2. Quad sets, hold for 5 seconds, 10 reps
3. Straight leg raises, 10 reps
4. Knee bends sitting over the edge of the bed, 10 reps each side
